notes.title: Fresh challenges and Steam Trading Cards are here!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! We’ve been working on the big update for the past few months and Today is the Day you can adventure the new game mods, as well as check out Urbo Steam Trading Cards.

[previewyoutube=klzra_B5QqY;full][/previewyoutube]
 
[h2]Sessional Mode[/h2]  
Prepare to put your skills to the ultimate test. Your moves are limited, so you will have to be chary of every move you make to grow your city to its fullest potential. For those who have that competitive spirit to be precise with every decision they take – this mode is worth trying.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/bbab8591ac41bb3f2a6a611b4650e31ee36de691.gif[/img]
 
[h2]Puzzle Mode[/h2]
This mode is an intriguing challenge with pre-set conditions. Your mission: delicately arrange each structure to eventually construct a level eight building in the center of an island. Here, a peaceful aura gently nudges you to explore various creative paths to achieve the goal. Crucially, in Puzzle mode you have the freedom to undo moves without restrictions. You can easily reset the island and try to solve the puzzle an entirely different way. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/13b0fa3f70b7ebd59803273aa3cbd263bbc5e0b5.gif[/img]

[h2]Urbo Steam Trading Cards![/h2]
We are pleased to introduce our trading cards which you can earn by playing the game. You can now gather Trading Cards, Craft Badges and display Profile Backgrounds/Emoticons from Urbo on Steam.

[h2]To conclude[/h2]
We hope that this update will provide you with a new warm-up for the mind. The optimal solutions for the new modes are now to be found. The sweet taste of victory awaits your grasp, as you embark on the journey to find your own perfect floating island where you will build the city of your dreams.
 
[i]You can see the full list of changes, additions, and fixes below:[/i]

Features:
[list]
[*] Two new game modes: Sessional Mode and Puzzle Mode;
[/list]General:
[list]
[*] Improved autosave system: it became faster and more reliable;
[*] UI and UX tweaks and improvements;
[*] Graphical settings window has returned on SteamDeck (may be useful if you connect an external monitor or TV to the console);
[/list]Bug fixes:
[list]
[*] Fixed rare crash cases;
[*] Fixed rare game freeze cases;
[*] Fixed minor issues with visual effects;
[*] Fixed a bug with sounds that were not affected by volume settings;
[*] Fixed other minor bugs and errors.
[/list]

notes.title: URBO: Upcoming Update and Fresh Challenges!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! We're pleased to announce the major update for URBO. Soon our game will delight you with brand new puzzles. Are you ready to join us on this amazing adventure? Here's what lies ahead:

[h1]Session Mode[/h1]
In this game mode, the number of moves is limited. If your goal is to reach the highest possible population, your every move truly counts. Sharpen your skills to become the architect of the most beautiful, prosperous city you can create in the Session Mode!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/bbab8591ac41bb3f2a6a611b4650e31ee36de691.gif[/img]

[h1]Puzzle Mode[/h1]
This mode is another fascinating puzzle with pre-set conditions. This time, your goal is to find the right place for each building from the queue to eventually construct a level eight building in the center of an island. You have quite a degree of freedom to get creative here. In Puzzle Mode, there is no restriction on undoing moves. In other words, you can return the island to its initial state and try to solve the puzzle in an entirely different way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/13b0fa3f70b7ebd59803273aa3cbd263bbc5e0b5.gif[/img]

The upcoming update will vary the gameplay and add depth to it. By removing the element of luck and keeping the core gameplay, we have created a new warm-up for the minds. After all, now puzzles have optimal solutions you have to find. If URBO lacked the feeling of victory, the upcoming update is exactly what you need. Hopefully, with the new game modes, you'll discover your own perfect floating island where you will build the city of your dreams.

Stay tuned, the update is far from release at this moment. But it's definitely worth the wait!

notes.title: Urbo review: Threes meets Dorfromantik in this chill puzzler
notes.notes:
After busting down the castle door with their chaotic, siege-based citybuilder Diplomacy Is Not An Option last year, the last thing I expected to see next from developers Door 407 was a chill, meditative puzzle game that's just about, well, building tiny cities. In Urbo there are no sky lasers, no oncoming hordes. Nothing. Just dinky little grid-based maps, and an endless stream of tiny adorable buildings to plonk down on them in the pursuit of sweet, sweet point scores.

This being a puzzle game, the aim here is to place three buildings of the same type altogether, either in a line or right-angled cluster, at which point they'll all shzooge together to level up to the next building type. This is where the Threes comparison comes in, though you can zhuzh more than three of the same building together if you're smart to earn more points. But it's not quite as simple as that. You see, your buildings will only shoump onto the tile you placed down last, and careful city planners will likely want to think about placing their buildings in reverse so they end up with their fancy new house in the place they actually want it, not in an awkward middle spot that cuts off two precious tiles from play, or awkwardly sits in the middle of another chain of dwellings accidentally. And yep, that's where the Dorfromantik connection comes in, and I really do like it very, very much.

notes.title: About gamepad support
notes.notes:
While developing URBO we tried to think of every possible situation in which you would want to spend time in our game. Some are more accustomed to play sitting in front of a monitor or a laptop. For someone it is important to be able to spend in URBO minutes on the road. There are those who like to relax and play on the couch in front of a big screen. We wanted to give you as much freedom as possible to choose under what circumstances you'd be more comfortable immersing in URBO. For this reason, it was impossible to avoid the issue of gamepad support. To summarize, the controls in URBO are fully adapted to play with controllers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/2368ac33f7d289748f5c2babd36f0d22cdfd63a5.png[/img]

notes.title: This citybuilding puzzle game is Threes meets Dorfromantik, and I'm extremely here for it
notes.notes:
I don't mean to alarm anyone, but I think Urbo might be my Dorfromantik of 2023. It's a chill, citybuilding puzzle game from the devs behind the altogether more violent Diplomacy Is Not An Option, and it's all about building tiny little villages on top of rocky outcrops. Except when you stick three of the same building type together, they all zhuup together to create an even bigger one. And a bigger one, and a bigger one. It's very satisfying. The smooshing lights up all the same parts of my brain that Threes did when I became obsessed with it about five years ago, while the tile planning hits scratches that big Dorfromantik itch, making for an excellent Steam Next Fest demo experience.

Also, we paid special attention to the performance and to how URBO looks on Steam Deck. For this last task, a separate graphics setup had to be designed. This allowed us to optimize the game for the console without significant visual losses.
URBO's Demo is already available, so if you have a Steam Deck - it's a nice time to give it a try.

notes.title: Dev blog. Buildings.
notes.notes:
In URBO, buildings are the main objects to interact with. Our main idea is to give you the freedom to choose both the architectural style and the scenery in which your city will be built. Therefore, when creating houses look, we need to consider not only their visual style but also how they fit into any surroundings. This is fair to environments already implemented in the game and those that exist only "on paper" so far.
It is also necessary to think about the set of houses in terms of progression. So that it feels like the buildings of the next level are slightly larger and more roomy than the buildings of the previous one. In addition, the playing field filled with houses of different levels should form a complete picture. It should look like a beautiful city divided into quarters.

*URBO is still in development, the visual aspects of the game may change in future

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/29dcf314fe20b40fce76f4d7bff24e946d88c3fa.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Dev. blog. The surroundings.
notes.notes:
From a visual point of view, the setting defines the overall mood and theme of the game world. Each environment, its natural area and entourage, is designed to assist your imagination. Looking at the surroundings, you can recreate the story of the place where you are building your town. Apparently, the setting must be in harmony with the sound.
We also faced the challenge of making it fit the game elements such as the buildings tyou place during the game. The entire picture should look natural and shouldn't raise any questions. It was also important for us to adjust the lighting and visuals so that the playing field looks "alive" even when you're not interacting with it.

*URBO is still in development, the visual aspects of the game may change in future

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/af33ea7c9dd62b6b2a98d64d24adbb7b84c12bd3.png[/img]

notes.title: Dev blog. Sound.
notes.notes:
Hey everyone.
Let's talk about sounds today. Similarly to music, sounds in games affect the level of immersion into virtual worlds. In addition, they notify players about their actions. When creating URBO, it was important for us to make sure that sounds would complement the picture enhancing the very feeling of the game flow.
Surround sounds should duplicate the visual information about the camera location. At the same time, they should blend in perfectly with the music. While being a part of the auditory background, event sounds should also signal the player's actions.

*URBO is still in development, the visual aspects of the game may change in future

[previewyoutube=kZmzTKX-NKw;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Dev blog. Music.
notes.notes:
Hey everyone.
Music is crucial for immersion in the game world. At the same time, it should not draw attention to much attention to itself. 
We had to choose music that would merge with the background, emphasizing the meditative atmosphere of the game. Also, we pursued a very uncommon effect: if you don't listen to it, you feel that there is no music in URBO at all. Conceptually, this is achieved by a careful track selection. The soundtrack of URBO includes music that is performed by a small number of instruments and that contains a minimum variety of external sounds.

*URBO is still in development, the visual aspects of the game may change in future

notes.title: Dev blog. Building queue and bonus points.
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, today we're talking about supporting game mechanics. 

In URBO, the houses to place on the map are shown in the queue part of the interface. So you can see the order and the level of houses that you will have to build on an island. For good placement, you gain bonus points. The better the move, the more buildings of one level turn into a building of the next level. As a result, you get more bonus points.

You can spend points on buying buildings of the desired level or on manipulations with the existing houses. Such as their removal or place change.
In short, this solution allows you to compensate for earlier mistakes and to redesign your islands. Thanks to bonus points, you can get more populated and beautiful towns by the end.

notes.title: Dev blog. Basic game mechanics.
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! Today in our story we will touch the URBO's core gameplay of URBO.
In our game, you will build beautiful cities with as many inhabitants as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/28a14b3c27c8784f46b9027dbe7154e1baa92959.gif[/img]

Buildings in a city come in different levels. If you build several buildings of the same level next to each other, they will turn into the building of the next level. This frees up space on the map. The higher the level of a building, the more people it can hold. In this way, different numbers of people may populate the same surface area in your city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/794c792c1a7860238ce500264bb8e9f1c41e3397.gif[/img]

When one island runs out of space, a new island appears in our world, with a different landscape and a different area for placing buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/dfc048cf9e8ca7cf3adef06b1f1d42d6a2b7feeb.gif[/img]

Once all the islands are built up, we can take look at the picturesque view we've got.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43166619/28a14b3c27c8784f46b9027dbe7154e1baa92959.gif[/img]

*URBO is still in development, the final appearance of the game may change

notes.title: Welcome to Urbo!
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=pYvHkXmbYxo;full][/previewyoutube]

Hello, friends! We are pleased to present you a simple puzzle game, "URBO", named after the Esperanto translation of the word 'city'.

Urbo is an atmospheric and meditative game. In it, you need to build cities in different sceneries, from primal jungles to post-apocalyptic wastelands. The larger your city, the more people live in it. It is the number of inhabitants that measures your success in URBO.  

You can already get an image of Urbo by watching our trailer. To give you something more, we announce that the game will have various levels that differ by size and playing field configuration. In spite of its apparent simplicity, Urbo is going to deliver a lot of fun to puzzle lovers.  

From this day forward we plan to post videos about the game and stories about its development. About what's coming to Urbo and what you shouldn't definitely expect from it. We'll be grateful to hear your first impressions, feedback, and suggestions. Please, feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.

Thank you, see you next time!
[i]Yours, Door 407 team.[/i]
